subject: Quantifying feature-level economics & procurement path for MedTech.ai
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@medtech.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — feature economics we discussed

Samir / team — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of the items we agreed to follow up on and the asks from your side so we can scope a unit-econ deep-dive: 

What we heard from you (confirm if any of this is off):
- Target integration: in-app triage + summarization + clinician-assist prompts (3 distinct features).
- Estimated activity: ~120M tokens / month initially; target growth to ~1B tokens / month over 12–18 months (you mentioned 3x by Q4).
- Target commercial threshold: you have a budget band of $8k–$20k / month for inference in initial pilot (procurement is conservative).
- Top metric: CAC payback for this feature must be < 9 months and feature-level gross margin target >= 60%.

Our immediate asks (what we need from you to model economics precisely):
1) Confirm active weekly MAU and expected conversion to paid feature (ballpark % helps).
2) Breakout of the 120M tokens across the three features (rough % split).
3) Any hard constraints from procurement on contract term / invoice cadence (annual pref with PO?).

What we'll deliver by next Wednesday:
- A feature-level unit-economic workbook that maps tokens -> $/1M tokens -> $/feature -> CAC payback run.
- 2 pricing options: conservative (lower unit cost, higher min commitment) and growth (lower commitment, higher $/token).
- A recommended procurement path with milestones for pilot -> expansion.

Next steps: please reply with the three quick points above. If you can share the budget PDF you mentioned we can encode that into the model (you can reply-all or drop into the shared link).

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: medtech_budget_v1.pdf (referenced)

From: Samir Patel <samir@medtech.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medtech.ai
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — feature economics we discussed

Vivek — thanks for the clear recap. Confirmations below: 

- MAU: ~45k MAU today; active session rate ~1.2 sessions/user/week. Expecting to reach ~200k MAU in 12 months with product-market fit investments.
- Token split: approximate now: triage 50%, summarization 30%, clinician-assist 20%. Could shift as we tune prompts.
- Procurement: pilot approval could be within 30 days; they prefer 6–12 month term for pilots with monthly invoices. PO processes vary by hospital partner (we'll need to coordinate).
- Budget: the $8k–$20k band is for the pilot phase. If we get clear $/feature metrics we can look to expand ASAP.

I've attached the high-level budget PDF (medtech_budget_v1.pdf) — it includes current marketing spend and an initial go-to-market plan that informs CAC expectations. Procurement will loop in legal next week for standard T&Cs.

Happy to jump on another 30m call once you share the initial workbook.

— Samir
Samir Patel, Head of Product
MedTech.ai

Attachment: medtech_budget_v1.pdf (attached by Samir)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo recap — feature economics we discussed

Looping internal owners — I can own the first-pass unit-econ workbook. Initial approach: 

- Tab 1: assumptions (MAU, sessions, conv %, tokens/session by feature) — populate from Samir's numbers.
- Tab 2: token-cost sensitivity (Redwood hosted: $/1M token breakouts by batch/quantization profile) — include 3 scenarios (Baseline 1.0, Quantized 8-bit, Aggressive cache/batching).
- Tab 3: $/feature calculation (tokens -> compute -> infra -> per-feature P&L).
- Tab 4: CAC payback schedule model: lifetime value assumptions + marketing spend allocations -> months to payback.

Questions for you, Vivek:
1) What is our target list price ranges to test? Samir asked for two packaging options — we should propose $/1M token bands and a per-feature seat/usage fee if appropriate.
2) Do we include potential quantization uplift in the pilot pricing (i.e., discounted rate once they commit to a dedicated inference pool)?

I'll prepare unit_econ_model_v0.1.xlsx and drop it in my draft folder. Planning to have a first-pass out by EOD today for your review, Vivek.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment: unit_econ_model_v0.1.xlsx (draft)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@medtech.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — feature economics we discussed

Samir — thanks, this is helpful. Ben — great plan. Couple of clarifications and the pricing bands I want to test with MedTech.ai: 

Clarifications for the model (Ben / Marissa please incorporate):
- Use Samir's MAU and the 50/30/20 token split baseline. For tokens/session use 1.8k tokens/session for triage, 600 tokens/session for summarization, 2.5k tokens/session for clinician-assist (these are conservative).
- Pilot volume for pricing sensitivity: model at 120M, 300M, 1B tokens/month.

Pricing bands to propose (two options):
1) Pilot-friendly (lower commitment): $1,800 / 1M tokens (hosted) with a soft commitment of 3 months and monthly invoice. No dedicated pool uplift.
2) Committed growth (preferred economics): $1,200 / 1M tokens with a 12-month minimum and options to enable a dedicated pool / quantized model (adds ~20% infrastructure efficiency).

Commercial asks for procurement: PO + 30 day net preferred; include simplified SLA for pilot. If procurement asks for credits up front, we can propose a small onboarding credit to accelerate sign-off (TBD).

Ben — prioritize producing: 1) a per-feature $/month at each volume tier, 2) CAC payback curves assuming CAC ranges in the attached budget (Samir's PDF), and 3) a short slide (1–2 pages) we can send to procurement summarizing the pilot commitment and expected outcomes.

Samir — propose we lock a 30m follow-up on Thursday to walk through the workbook. I added a tentative Meet: https://meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij. If that works, Ben will present the model and we can agree on next steps for procurement.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
